name: You Too Good.
summary: Lumak sends you from Orgrimmar to seek his friend Nat Pagle. Your skill has outgrown ordinary lessons, and Nat camps on a distant islet south of Theramore Isle.

sections.title: Lumak's Limits
sections.body: Lumak teaches fishers in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. He sees you have learned all he can teach about rod and reel. So he admits you are too good for ordinary lessons. Artisan fishing calls for knowledge beyond the city and the Horde.

sections.title: An Unlikely Friendship
sections.body: Lumak sends you to find his human friend, Nat Pagle. Though the Horde and Alliance clash across Kalimdor, he warns you not to harm or eat Nat. Nat camps on an islet in Dustwallow Marsh, south of Theramore Isle. He keeps clear of politics and cares only whether the fish are biting.

faq.q: Who sends me on this quest?
aliases: where to get you too good
faq.answer: Lumak, the fishing trainer in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, sends you when your skill has grown beyond expert.
Nat Pagle camps on an islet off the coast of Dustwallow Marsh, south of Theramore Isle.

faq.q: Why does an orc have a human friend?
aliases: why is nat pagle friends with an orc
faq.answer: Lumak and Nat Pagle became friends through fishing. Their shared passion crosses the bitter rivalry between orcs and humans.

faq.q: What happens when I speak to Nat Pagle?
faq.answer: Nat Pagle gives you a demanding trial. You travel across Azeroth and catch rare fish before he teaches you further.

faq.q: Is Theramore safe for Horde to pass through?
aliases: getting to nat pagle as horde
faq.answer: No. Theramore is a fortress town guarded by the Alliance. To reach Nat's island, skirt the coast or detour around town to avoid the guards.

faq.q: Why can't Lumak train me further himself?
faq.answer: Lumak has taught you all he knows. Nat Pagle can teach you artisan fishing, and anglers across the known world regard him as a legend.

angles.text: Even during the faction war, people can form bonds across its lines through a shared craft or pastime.
As an orc, you can see Lumak's patience, good humor, and respect for nature in his friendship across enemy lines.
